subject: Smaller degrees of freedom for the Scalar invariance model than that of the Metric one?

messages.author: d2b0929e2443470b
messages.subject: Smaller degrees of freedom for the Scalar invariance model than that of the Metric one?
parts:
Hello everyone,
 
I am trying to test the measurement invariance in my bi-factor model with CFA tests. I have 23 binary questions coded "correct" and "incorrect" and 3 different groups in my data. The sample sizes are approximately 200 for each group.
To test the measurement invariance, I have followed the Van de Schoot et al. (2012) step-by-step process where progressively constrained models are compared. I have estimated the configural, metric and scalar model. The test statistics, fit indices and model results all seem good and reasonable. However, when I estimate the Scalar model, results give smaller degrees of freedom than the metric model.
Is there a possible reason for this? I couldn't find anything in the internet although I looked for it carefully. Can someone please assist me to find the reason or help me to find a reference to have a better understanding?

Here are the codes that I run. 
### configural model ### 
model_mck_bifactor_con_2 <- 'MCK =~ Q1+Q2A+Q3B+Q3C+Q5+Q6+Q8A+Q8B+Q8C+Q10+Q12B+Q13A+Q13B+Q13C+Q17A+Q18B+Q19A+Q19B+Q19C+Q19D+Q20A+Q22+Q23
Q8 =~ Q8A+Q8B+Q8C; Q13 =~ Q13A+Q13B+Q13C; Q19 =~ Q19A+Q19B+Q19C+Q19D;
MCK~~0*Q8; MCK~~0*Q13; MCK~~0*Q19;
Q8~~0*Q13; Q8~~0*Q19; Q13~~0*Q19
Q3B ~~ Q19A+Q19B+Q19C+Q19D; Q3C ~~ Q19A+Q19B+Q19C+Q19D; Q3B ~~ Q3C'
### Q3 and Q19 are theoretically correlated. ###

cfa.configural.mck.bifactor_2 <- cfa(model_mck_bifactor_con_2, data = data_mck, estimator = "WLSMV", ordered=T, group = "COUNTRY",
                                     missing="pairwise", parameterization="delta")

### metric model ### 
cfa.metric.mck.bifactor <- cfa(model_mck_bifactor_con_2, data = data_mck, estimator = "WLSMV", ordered=T, group = "COUNTRY", missing="pairwise",
  parameterization="delta", group.equal="loadings")
summary(cfa.metric.mck.bifactor, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

### scalar model ### 
cfa.scalar.mck.bifactor <- cfa(model_mck_bifactor_con_2, data = data_mck, estimator = "WLSMV", ordered=T, group = "COUNTRY", missing="pairwise",
                               parameterization="delta", group.equal=c("loadings","thresholds"))

Below is the compareFit test results. As you can see, the scalar model has smaller Df.



Thanks a lot in advance. 
I wish everyone a good and productive day.
Best Regards,
Enes.

The scalar model still yields fewer degrees of freedom than the metric model. As far as I know, the more constrained scalar model should methodologically give higher degrees of freedom. messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Smaller degrees of freedom for the Scalar invariance model than that of the Metric one?
parts: when I estimate the Scalar model, results give smaller degrees of freedom than the metric model.

Because the models aren't nested: https://doi.org/10.1007/s11336-016-9506-0
Loadings aren't comparable unless the latent responses of indicators share a common scale, which requires FIRST constraining their thresholds to equality.
But you can't even disentangle differences in thresholds, loadings, or intercepts when indicators have only 1 threshold to equate. So you can only compare the default configural model directly to the scalar-invariance model, as an omnibus test of scalar invariance.
